jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Budget Pottery
jokes.joke: I got into pottery because I'm cheap. I thought, why pay $18 for a mug when I can pay $90 for a class, ruin a Saturday, and make one that looks like it was dug up behind a kindergarten? Now guests pick it up and say, "Did you make this?" which is just polite for, "Is it safe?"

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Ancient Critique
jokes.joke: I took one of those historical walking tours where the guide keeps stopping at empty lots to describe buildings that burned down in 1887. Forty minutes in, I realized the whole tour is just a cheap guy with Google and a blazer. He pointed at a Walgreens and said, 'This was once the site of a magnificent opera house.' Sir, that is a Walgreens. It still is.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: The Anniversary Vase
jokes.joke: I’m incredibly stingy. I refused to pay eighty bucks for a vase for my wife’s birthday, so I decided to take up glassblowing and just make her one. It’s been two years. I’ve spent fifteen thousand dollars on a blast furnace in the garage, I have absolutely no eyebrows left, and I just handed her something that looks exactly like a melted Jolly Rancher.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Cheapskate Pit Stop
jokes.joke: I pulled into this truck stop last week because I'm stingy and the gas was three cents cheaper. Grabbed a coffee, got to the register, and started counting out exact change like it was the national debt. The cashier just stared and said, 'Buddy, at this rate the only thing you're hauling is disappointment down the highway. Next time just siphon the pump and save us both the trouble.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Stingy Craft
jokes.joke: I tried taking a pottery class, but I’m so stingy the instructor pulled me aside. She said, “Clay is cheap—use more than a thimble.” I told her I was just being artistic. She said, “No, you’re making a shot glass for a mouse.” Honestly, the only thing I’ve truly shaped is her disappointment.

scores.comment: Clear premise and decent stage rhythm, but the payoff is more wry than laugh-heavy; stingy/cheap concept is present but slightly indirect.
Strong escalation from saving money to ruinous DIY expense, with a clean concrete final image; the best constructed joke in the batch.
Understandable setup, but the cashier dialogue feels written rather than overheard, and the punchline leans on phrasing more than a real turn.
The mouse shot glass is a solid comic image, but the final disappointment line is familiar and softens the landing.

The math inversion (cheap -> expensive) is the right premise, 'dug up behind a kindergarten' is a strong image, and 'Is it safe?' lands cleanly as the final beat. Efficient construction, natural voice, no wasted words.

Same stingy-craftsman inversion but escalated to absurdist extremes. The blast furnace and missing eyebrows earn their place; 'melted Jolly Rancher' is a genuinely funny closer. Slightly looser than A but the escalation compensates.

The setup is sound but the cashier's punchline is overlong, writerly, and reads as someone narrating a joke rather than delivering one. 'Hauling disappointment down the highway' tries too hard. The comic payoff deflates under the wordcount.

'Shot glass for a mouse' is the best line and does real work. The final beat ('shaped her disappointment') is clever but slightly expected once you see it coming. Solid filler; doesn't quite break into genuinely good territory.
Strong rhythm and escalation. The final punchline is natural and carries a genuine laugh, though the core premise is slightly familiar.
Good observational setup. The turn is solid, though the final tag 'It still is' slightly dampens the punchline's momentum.
Relies heavily on unnatural, overwrought dialogue. The cashier's response sounds like an AI template rather than human speech.
The 'shot glass for a mouse' visual is decent, but ending on the 'shaped her disappointment' trope is a very generic, recognizable AI joke shape.
Relatable cheap-craft premise with safe mug turn; solid but familiar angle.
Strong visual of empty-lot tour and Walgreens punch; natural escalation.
Clear stingy-to-disaster escalation with strong final image; good rhythm.
Tiny clay joke lands mildly; disappointment tag feels expected.
Clean pottery angle with a tidy final line; mild but real humor.
Good observational turn; Walgreens callback lands steadily.
Strong escalation and a clear payoff; solid, not standout.
Decent truck-stop framing with a workable closing line.
